value.rationale: The beta-Hausdorff matrix is a canonical measure-induced summability operator. The unnormalized squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm is an intrinsic finite matrix/spectral invariant and an aggregate urn-count collision probability. A complete sharp three-regime classification over all positive shapes, with explicitly evaluated constants and a uniform two-parameter crossover profile, resolves a natural singular threshold. It has recognizable test cases (arcsine and classical Cesàro), not an arbitrary parameter slice.
